findings.claim: Permission check isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) collapses to owner-only; team ADMINs who are not organizer/attendee get FORBIDDEN despite the variable name isTeamAdminOrOwner.
findings.evidence: isTeamAdmin (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284) already matches ADMIN or OWNER; isTeamOwner (:286-295) matches OWNER only. Repo convention is role === OWNER || role === ADMIN (confirm.handler.ts:127-128, get.handler.ts:405-406). Reasoned; repro: ADMIN member of the event type's team calls addGuests and gets FORBIDDEN.
findings.reason: Raised by all four seats with consistent source citations; use isTeamAdmin alone (also drops one DB query).

findings.claim: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS filter is bypassable by case change or +alias; existing-attendee de-dup is also case-sensitive, so A@x.com is added beside a@x.com.
findings.evidence: Blacklist entries are lowercased but the raw guest is compared with includes(guest); extractBaseEmail never applied. handleNewBooking.ts:741-745 and checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts:17-18 normalise with extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase(). Reasoned; repro: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=bad@x.com, guests: ['Bad@x.com'] or ['bad+1@x.com'] is inserted and emailed.
findings.reason: Abuse-control bypass against an established codebase convention; three correctness/spec seats concur.

findings.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disable-host/attendee-email settings; handler does not pass booking.eventType?.metadata.
findings.evidence: Sibling senders gate on eventTypeDisableHostEmail / eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail (sendLocationChangeEmails email-manager.ts:495-523, sendScheduledSeatsEmails :248/:260). The new function takes no metadata; handler line 168 passes none. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Breaks a documented sibling convention; event types that disabled standard emails (e.g. platform/workflows) still get Cal.com emails.

findings.claim: Guest list has no server-side size cap and no server-side uniqueness check; only the client dialog refines uniqueness, so a direct tRPC call can create duplicate attendee rows and send unbounded mail in the organizer's name.
findings.evidence: ZAddGuestsInputSchema has no .max() and no uniqueness refine; createMany at handler:83-91 inserts duplicates; emails go out with from: organizer name / replyTo organizer email. Reasoned; repro: guests: ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] via tRPC creates two attendee rows.
findings.reason: Spam/abuse path at a trust boundary; add .max(N) and a case-insensitive uniqueness refine.

findings.claim: Server never checks booking status or time: guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, sending REQUEST/CONFIRMED ICS invites that revive dead meetings on recipients' calendars.
findings.evidence: UI gates the action on isUpcoming && !isCancelled (BookingListItem.tsx:544-554), but the handler accepts any booking id; attendee-add-guests-email.ts:10-17 and organizer-add-guests-email.ts:14-20 emit method REQUEST, status CONFIRMED. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Server must enforce what the UI assumes; reject non-active / past bookings.

findings.claim: Seated events (seatsPerTimeSlot): attendees are created without BookingSeat rows, bypassing the seat limit, and any single seat-holder (isAttendee) can add guests and push the full attendee list to the organizer's calendar, exposing seat-holders to each other even with seatsShowAttendees=false.
findings.evidence: Handler creates Attendee rows via createMany with no seat handling; isAttendee check at :52-54 admits any seat holder; updateCalendarAttendees pushes evt.attendees. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Privacy and capacity breach on seated events; smallest fix is to refuse addGuests for seated bookings server-side.

findings.claim: addGuests uses plain authedProcedure with a custom check instead of bookingsProcedure: any logged-in attendee may add guests, while COLLECTIVE co-hosts (allowed by bookingsProcedure/editLocation) are now refused.
findings.evidence: bookingsProcedure (bookings/util.ts:19-63) admits organizer or COLLECTIVE host; addGuests.handler.ts:46-56 admits organizer, attendee by email match, or team owner. Reasoned; no spec states the intended model.
findings.reason: Who may add guests (attendees? collective hosts?) is a product decision with no spec; the abuse impact is bounded by the accepted size-cap/blacklist/status fixes. Settle with the PR author; check: collective co-host calls addGuests and gets FORBIDDEN.

findings.claim: Handler passes raw guests instead of uniqueGuests to sendAddGuestsEmails, so a re-submitted existing attendee gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice.
findings.evidence: email-manager.ts:541-545 sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to every attendee whose email is in newGuests. Reasoned.
findings.reason: One-token fix; all four seats noted it.

findings.claim: evt is built without team, so the team-member branch in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs and team hosts are never notified.
findings.evidence: calendarEvent.team?.members at email-manager.ts:531-537 is always undefined because evt (handler:124-147) sets no team. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Dead branch means a missing notification; populate team or drop the branch.

findings.claim: onError message is a template string that is never falsy, so the unable_to_add_guests fallback never shows and users see raw 'CODE: key' strings.
findings.evidence: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` || t('unable_to_add_guests') — left side always truthy. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Dead fallback plus user-visible raw error codes.

findings.claim: Handler throws FORBIDDEN with message key you_do_not_have_permission, which is not defined in en/common.json; users see the raw key.
findings.evidence: grep '"you_do_not_have_permission"' apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json returns nothing at the patch head (orchestrator check); thrown at addGuests.handler.ts:55.
findings.reason: Confirmed by grep.

findings.claim: Dialog state bugs: isInvalidEmail never reset on success or on overlay/Esc close; closing via onOpenChange keeps old emails; removing all fields makes Add a silent no-op; client uniqueness check is case-sensitive.
findings.evidence: Only the Cancel button resets state (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:88-93,114); handleAdd returns early with no feedback when list is empty (:48-58). Reasoned.
findings.reason: Cheap UX correctness fixes in new code.

findings.claim: No transaction/compensation: attendees are written before updateCalendarAttendees, which is not wrapped; if it throws, DB has the guests, no emails go out, and a retry fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid. Concurrent requests can both pass de-dup. Email-send catch drops err.
findings.evidence: createMany at :83-91 precedes updateCalendarAttendees at :163-165 with no try; catch at :170 logs a fixed string. Reasoned.
findings.reason: ponytail: partial-failure handling matches editLocation's existing pattern; revisit if calendar-provider failures are observed. Check: make updateCalendarAttendees throw and retry the same request.

findings.claim: EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials, not the organizer's; references without credentialId (and other_calendar refs) are matched against the caller's calendars when an attendee or owner adds guests.
findings.evidence: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) at :160; EventManager.ts:872-878 matches by caller credentials when reference.credentialId is absent. The OCR seat examined this and declined to report it because updateAllCalendarEvents falls back to reference.credentialId. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Seats disagree on impact; settle with a test where a non-organizer adds guests to a booking whose reference has no credentialId and assert the organizer's calendar event is updated.

findings.claim: New guests are saved with name '' and inherit the organizer's timeZone/locale, so emails and calendar entries show blank names.
findings.evidence: createMany data at :83-88. Reasoned.
findings.reason: ponytail: defensible default with no spec; revisit if blank names are reported.

findings.claim: New authenticated mutation that writes to the DB, calls external calendars and sends email ships with zero tests (no handler integration test for permissions/blacklist/de-dup, no E2E for the dialog); data-testid='add_members' is added but unused.
findings.evidence: No test files in the patch; apps/web/playwright/bookings-list.e2e.ts is the natural home. CONTRIBUTING.md does not mandate tests (mattpocock seat).
findings.reason: Each accepted fix above lands with a red-then-green guard test in the fix rounds, which covers the handler's permission/blacklist/de-dup matrix.

findings.claim: showAttendees is never passed to AttendeeScheduledEmail, so seated events with seatsShowAttendees=true hide the attendee list in these emails.
findings.evidence: Constructor inherited from attendee-scheduled-email.ts:19-26; email-manager.ts:542/544 omit the argument. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Moot once seated bookings are refused by the accepted seated-event fix; revisit if addGuests is later enabled for seated events.

findings.claim: findFirst include pulls user.credentials (full credential keys) that are never read, and include: {x: true} trips @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true.
findings.evidence: Credentials actually come from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) at :160; include block copied from bookingsProcedure util.ts:48-58. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Drop credentials: true — stops loading secrets that are never used.

findings.claim: MultiEmail is a near-verbatim copy of the multiemail factory in packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:231-308 (which carries //TODO: Make it a ui component); the original was not switched over, so two copies already drift (array mutation, data-testids, htmlFor).
findings.evidence: Side-by-side comparison by two seats. Reasoned. Normalised from Important (ponytail) to Minor: duplication, no behaviour defect; advisory seats.
findings.reason: ponytail: switching form-builder to the ui component changes e2e test IDs (add-another-guest) outside this PR's scope; do it as a follow-up.

findings.claim: Second prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow refetches the organizer already loaded via booking.user.
findings.evidence: include user at :36-41 vs findFirstOrThrow at :58-68; same habit exists in editLocation.handler.ts:32. Reasoned.
findings.reason: ponytail: one redundant query, copies an existing pattern; fold into a later cleanup.

findings.claim: ~40 lines of CalendarEvent building duplicated from editLocation.handler.ts:57-95.
findings.evidence: Only location and conferenceCredentialId differ. Reasoned.
findings.reason: ponytail: no shared helper exists; extracting one now is speculative abstraction.

findings.claim: credentials: [...credentials] copies an array for no reason.
findings.evidence: Spread of an array that is not mutated afterwards. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Cosmetic; no behaviour or measurable cost, not worth a diff line in the review surface.

findings.claim: Zod validation schema is rebuilt on every render.
findings.evidence: Schema with refine declared inside the component body. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Negligible cost in a dialog, no behaviour change; not worth review surface.

findings.claim: Lazy wrapper is unnecessary and its '40kb' comment is copied from PhoneInputLazy/AddressInputLazy where it is true.
findings.evidence: MultiEmail only uses components @calcom/ui already ships. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Follows the house pattern for form inputs exported from @calcom/ui (PhoneInputLazy, AddressInputLazy); removing it needs import rewiring to avoid a barrel cycle (per the seat itself) for no user-visible defect.

coverage: Files skipped: none — all 15 patch files reviewed by all four seats; en/common.json, packages/ui/index.tsx, MultiEmailLazy.tsx and the emails/src/templates wrappers were only skimmed by some seats; other locales not assessed (Crowdin-managed).
